narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your current job. Because this probability tips above 50%, the system recommends denying your promotion to reduce the risk of investing in someone likely to depart soon.

Three factors drove this prediction, ranked by importance. First, having received other job opportunities while at the company strongly pushed the model toward predicting you will leave. Employees predicted to stay rarely report such external offers, so this signal carried the heaviest weight. Second, your 6–10 years in your current role worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying; most employees the model expects to remain have shorter tenure here. Third, your overall career experience of more than 11 years also nudged the outcome slightly toward leaving, as very experienced professionals in the dataset are somewhat more likely to move on.

Taken together, the pull from external opportunities outweighed the stabilizing effect of your long service. The organization should discuss with you whether those outside offers remain active and explore ways to strengthen your sense of future growth internally. You may wish to reflect on what would make staying feel more secure and rewarding before deciding on next steps. (218 words)
